In Ableton/Live, the MIDI Ports list in the MIDI settings shows every MIDI port the computer offers, once as an input (In:) and once as an output (Out:) (Ableton/Live/UG/17 Routing and IO/03 External MIDI In-Out/01 MIDI Port Inputs and Outputs).
Four switches decide what Live does with each side of a port:
Track — carries notes and CC between the port and Live's tracks, for a track's MIDI From or MIDI To.
Four switches decide what Live does with each side of a port:
Sync — sends or receives MIDI Clock. An output with Sync on also shows MIDI Clock Sync Delay and MIDI Clock Type (Ableton/Live/UG/37 Sync with Link Tempo Follower and MIDI/03 Synchronizing via MIDI).
Four switches decide what Live does with each side of a port:
Remote — lets a controller on the port map to Live's parameters, and sends feedback back out (Ableton/Live/UG/34 MIDI and Key Remote/01 MIDI Remote Control/02 Manual Control Surface Setup).
Four switches decide what Live does with each side of a port:
MPE — inputs only; treats the port as an MPE controller (Ableton/Live/UG/12 Editing MPE).

How can the Claude/Code command line connect to Ableton/Live/ProducerPal?

Short answer: register Producer Pal as an MCP server with claude mcp add, or install Producer Pal's Agent Skill. Either way the Producer Pal device has to be running in the open Live Set, and its server listens on port 3350.

Can a script make Ableton/Live 11, 12, or 13 reselect the Zoom H5 as its audio interface after I unplug and replug it?

Short answer: not through any Ableton API. The audio device lives in Live's Settings (Preferences.cfg), not in the Set, and nothing Ableton documents lets a script change it. The workarounds below avoid the reset or make it quicker.

What Live 11.3.43 did on this Mac, from ~/Library/Preferences/Ableton/Live 11.3.43/Log.txt:

The H5 reports a different CoreAudio UniqueId in each audio interface mode: …:H5:000000000000:2,1 in Stereo mode (2 in) and …:H5:000000000000:1,2 in Multi Track mode (4 in). Live probably treats these as two different devices, so a setting saved in one mode would not match the other. This is inferred from the log, not tested.

Why a script can't set it:
Can a script make Ableton/Live 11, 12, or 13 reselect the Zoom H5 as its audio interface after I unplug and replug it?

The Live Object Model's Application object has version, dialog, CPU-load and control-surface members, and no audio device property (LOM: Application). Python remote scripts and Max for Live both go through this object model.

Why a script can't set it:
Preferences.cfg is a binary file with no published format. Editing it is unsupported and could reset all your Settings.
Can a script make Ableton/Live 11, 12, or 13 reselect the Zoom H5 as its audio interface after I unplug and replug it?
Why a script can't set it:

Ableton forum threads ask for Live to reconnect a returning interface or to remember a preferred device. Neither request has an Ableton answer saying the feature exists (Always revert to preferred audio interface when connected?, Reconnect Audio Interface).

Why a script can't set it:
Can a script make Ableton/Live 11, 12, or 13 reselect the Zoom H5 as its audio interface after I unplug and replug it?
Keep the H5 in one mode. Pick Multi Track or Stereo on the H5 and use it every time, so the H5 always shows Live the same device (Zoom H5/UI/Mode/4-Audio-Interface).
Can a script make Ableton/Live 11, 12, or 13 reselect the Zoom H5 as its audio interface after I unplug and replug it?

Plug in the H5 before launching Live. Settings were last saved at 18:48 on 2026-11-18 Wed with the H5 selected, and Live reads them at launch. If the H5 drops mid-session, saving the Set and relaunching Live should restore it. Not yet tested here.
Can a script make Ableton/Live 11, 12, or 13 reselect the Zoom H5 as its audio interface after I unplug and replug it?

Live 12 and later, output only: the output chooser has a Use System Device option that follows the device chosen in macOS Sound settings (Live 12 manual, 2.3.3 Audio). macOS usually switches its output to a USB audio device when one is plugged in. Even then, the manual describes the option for output only, so the H5 input would still need picking by hand. Live 11 does not have this option.
